claims.text: The material is an as-designed, high-performance multicomponent high-entropy alloy.
A controlled, optimized thermal treatment is the proposed intervention.
The optimized thermal treatment will reduce post-exposure toughness degradation.
The thermal treatment will stabilize the alloy's grain structure and grain boundaries.
The thermal treatment will prevent deleterious phase transformations.
Deleterious intermetallic or phase formation can impair mechanical performance.
Grain-boundary stabilization and suppression of deleterious transformations will preserve toughness after heating.
The treatment will retain the original strength–ductility combination after service-relevant heating.
The proposed treatment and exposure temperature range is 500–800°C.
The proposed treatment and exposure duration is 1–10 hours.
The proposed loading boundary is minimal or no external stress.
The comparator is an untreated alloy with identical composition and processing history.
Toughness, microstructure, and tensile properties can be compared between treated and untreated specimens.
Significantly lower toughness in the treated alloy than in the untreated baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
Any altered microstructure in the treated alloy relative to the untreated baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis expects treatment-induced stabilization of grain structure and phase composition, which may itself produce a microstructure different from the untreated baseline, but the falsification rule treats any altered microstructure as falsifying.
